note: Ids, contracts, tiers, rationale and seed provenance only; no fixture content or credential value.

revisions.item: benign public-identifier: NRAK- user API key as a sibling attribution control
revisions.reason: NRAK- is the contracted must-redact family new-relic-user-api-key (T1). A non-twin control is scored unscoped (benchmarks/lib/lattice.ts scoreRow: any finding flags it), so it would assert silence on another family's secret; family-scoped scoring exists only for twins.

revisions.item: benign near-miss: 40-character hex value beside newrelic
revisions.reason: The contract review records a still-issued legacy all-hex 40-character license key outside the pattern and New Relic's own page still calls the key a 40-character hex string; silence on a 40-hex value beside newrelic is provider-undecided and cannot be a negative expectation (decision-stop-asserting-provider-undecided-format-properties).

revisions.item: benign encoded-value: base64 of a license key in a Secret data: field
revisions.reason: The contract states no policy for an encoded license key, so a silence expectation on the Base64 of a live-shaped key would be asserted, not evidenced.

revisions.item: benign public-identifier: Mailchimp Transactional (Mandrill) key
revisions.reason: No provider-owned source for the Mandrill key shape was established in this pass (the ledger's own drop condition), and as a live secret in an unscoped control it would assert global silence on a credential.

revisions.item: benign near-miss: 40-hex commit id beside deepgram; benign encoded-value: sha1 beside a deepgram model name
revisions.reason: The contract admits any 40-hex value beside a same-line deepgram name, so silence there would be asserted, not evidenced — the exclusion #384e already recorded for this family (fixtures/generated/beta8/384e.mjs header).

revisions.item: twin context:keyword (ASSEMBLYAI_API_KEY in the HTTPie template)
revisions.reason: The HTTPie positive's gate is the api.deepgram.com host, not a keyword, so a keyword swap there mutates nothing; the same one-property keyword swap is authored on the docker run -e positive, whose only gate is DEEPGRAM_API_KEY.

revisions.item: benign near-miss: 64-character image digest on a confluentinc/ line
revisions.reason: The contract admits any 64-character [A-Za-z0-9+/] value beside a same-line confluent keyword, and confluentinc contains it; silence there would be asserted, not evidenced.

revisions.item: twin context:pairing (key-id half removed)
revisions.reason: The contract's gate is the confluent keyword, not the key-id pairing; removing the key id leaves the value gated, so the twin would mutate no contract property.

revisions.item: benign encoded-value: MD5 beside a twilio dependency name
revisions.reason: The contract admits a 32-hex value beside the word twilio, so silence there would be asserted, not evidenced.

revisions.item: twins context:pairing and context:host on the userinfo URL
revisions.reason: The contract names two alternative gates (a same-line Account SID or the word twilio); the userinfo URL carries both, so removing either one leaves the other and neither mutation removes the gate.

revisions.item: benign near-miss: 40-alphanumeric integrity-like token on a cohere package line
revisions.reason: The contract admits any 40-alphanumeric value after a same-line cohere name; the #384e exclusion for this family applies.

revisions.item: twin context:host (Java builder pointed at another host)
revisions.reason: The Java positive's gate is the Cohere builder itself; changing a host would leave the value gated, and adding a host to the positive would give it two gates.

revisions.item: twin boundary (identifier character after the Go const value)
revisions.reason: The body is open-length [A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}; a trailing identifier character extends a still-valid key, so the twin is not lexically separable (docs/decisions/2026-09-21-check-lexical-separability.md).

revisions.item: benign near-miss: ABSK with a head that decodes to another label; twin head (one head character changed)
revisions.reason: The contract review states that an ABSK-only key with another head is a T2 shape it does not assert either way and that no fixture asserts silence on a head-less ABSK value.

revisions.item: twins padding (three '=') and boundary (trailing identifier character)
revisions.reason: The body is open-length standard Base64 with optional padding; both mutated values still contain an isolated contract-valid key (the '=' ends the match), so neither twin is lexically separable.

revisions.item: benign public-identifier: sk-proj- project key as a sibling attribution control
revisions.reason: sk-proj- is the contracted must-redact family openai-token; an unscoped control would assert silence on another family's secret.

revisions.item: twins context:scheme, context:field (commented example) and context:key (DOCS_EXAMPLE_URL)
revisions.reason: The contract is 'password in userinfo of a URI' and its twin source (RFC 3986) names only the ':' and '@' delimiters; a scheme swap, a comment marker or a variable rename leaves userinfo intact and mutates no contract property.

revisions.item: benign public-identifier: whsec_ signing secret as a sibling attribution control
revisions.reason: whsec_ is the contracted T1 must-redact family stripe-webhook-signing-secret (#372); an unscoped control would assert silence on it.

revisions.item: twin mode (sk_prod_)
revisions.reason: The pinned gitleaks 8.30.1 stripe rule admits a prod mode and Stripe's key page does not state that no other mode is issued, so the property is disputed and no provider decides it.

revisions.item: benign placeholder sk_test_ + 32 X
revisions.reason: 32 X characters satisfy the frozen T1 pattern and fail lexical separability; the documentation placeholder is authored with 24 x characters.

revisions.item: benign public-identifier pk_live_ tier
revisions.reason: The ledger calls it a T1 control; the reviewed Beta.8 control rules score every non-twin public-identifier control at T2 (T1 controls require a twin with a provider source), so it lands at T2 without any contract change.

revisions.item: benign public-identifier: github_pat_ as a sibling attribution control
revisions.reason: github_pat_ is the contracted must-redact family github-fine-grained-pat (#371); an unscoped control would assert silence on it.

revisions.item: twin boundary (identifier character after the AA tail)
revisions.reason: Dropped after the first scan, on contract text alone: the contract review states that no length, alphabet or tail twin is authored on the tool-only 93 + AA field and that the product keeps a >= 20 byte superset, so a trailing identifier character asserts an undecided length property. Dropped together with the stripe and github trailing twins, whatever each scored.

revisions.item: twin boundary (identifier character after the 32-character body)
revisions.reason: Dropped after the first scan, on rule text alone: the pinned trufflehog 3.97.4 stripe rule matches [rs]k_live_[a-zA-Z0-9]{20,247} and gitleaks 8.30.1 (sk|rk)_(test|live|prod)_[a-zA-Z0-9]{10,99}, and the contract review calls the body length un-probeable, so a 33-character body is disputed, not tool-undisputed as the ledger recorded.

revisions.item: twin boundary (identifier character after the 36-character body)
revisions.reason: Dropped after the first scan, on rule text alone: the pinned trufflehog 3.97.4 github rule matches (ghp|gho|ghu|ghs|ghr|github_pat)_[a-zA-Z0-9_]{36,255}, so a 37-character body is disputed by a pinned peer, not tool-undisputed as the ledger recorded. This twin scored clean; it is dropped for the same reason as the two that did not.

revisions.item: benign placeholder ghp_ + 36 x
revisions.reason: 36 x characters satisfy the frozen T1 pattern and fail lexical separability; the placeholder is authored with 20 x characters.
